subject: Hosting decision anchors: VPC/on-prem gating items for Lifeline Health
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@lifelinehealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Bauer <tom.bauer@lifelinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — hosting options and constraints

Aditya — thanks for the call earlier. I wanted to capture the bits that matter for our infra/security review so we don't lose anything in follow-up. Below is my summary — please correct anything I missed.

Summary of Lifeline's top constraints and objectives:
- Data residency: PHI must remain within our AWS GovCloud account and not traverse public internet egress from any external service.
- Connectivity: Preferred model is VPC peering or PrivateLink into our account. Transit gateways may be allowed with our network team's approval but need an architecture diagram.
- Air-gap scenarios: For certain pilots we may require an isolated environment (no outbound internet except to Redwood-managed egress via approved proxies).
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) mandatory for production; will need documentation of key-handling and rotation.
- Audit & evidence: Access logs, request traces, and a tamper-evident audit trail for 12 months. SOC2 & penetration test evidence required.

Questions / asks from Lifeline team:
1) Can Redwood run as a private control plane with compute residing in our account? If not, what network patterns do you support (VPC peering, PrivateLink, transit)?
2) For a VPC-hosted deployment, what ports/protocols and CIDR ranges do you need?
3) Does Redwood support customer KMS with HSM-backed keys for token encryption and model cache encryption?
4) In an air-gapped pilot, what is the minimum footprint (CPU/GPU) and how do you handle software updates/patching?

Attachments: I attached a rough network diagram and our security requirements spreadsheet.

Next steps we proposed on the call: Lifeline will share a network contact (Tom) and a list of compliance docs we need; Redwood to provide an architecture sketch and a short checklist for the VPC/on-prem options.

Thanks —
Priya
Director, Cloud Security
Lifeline Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@lifelinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — hosting options and constraints

Priya — this is a good concise capture, thanks. I added a few clarifications inline and laid out the immediate next deliveries from our side.

Clarifications / Redwood posture:
- Private control plane: We offer a Private deployment model where the control plane can be run as a managed service with compute deployed into customer VPCs. This is our recommended pattern for regulated PHI workloads.
- Network patterns: We support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and an approved Transit Gateway pattern. In all cases we publish a minimal egress list (CIDR ranges + ports) and an architecture sketch for review.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS is supported for all persistent secrets and model cache encryption; HSM integration is available for Enterprise Private deployments — we'll provide KMS integration docs.
- Audit / logs: We can provide per-request logs, model call traces, and a 12-month retention export for audit. We will need to discuss log delivery (S3 push vs. customer-side pull).

Immediate deliverables from Redwood (I own these):
1) Architecture sketch showing Private control plane + compute in Lifeline VPC (ETA: 48 business hours).
2) Minimal egress/ports + recommended CIDR ranges (ETA: 24 business hours).
3) KMS/HSM integration doc and cert matrix (ETA: 3 business days).
4) Short runbook for air-gapped pilot: baseline footprint, update/patch process, and packaging options (ETA: 5 business days).

Ben, Monica — I'm looping you for network and procurement context. Ben, can you flag runtime sizing options (GPU/CPU) for an initial 1k qps pilot and an air-gapped footprint? Monica, please prepare the procurement checklist and expected SOW items.

Proposed next meeting: Wed 2028-08-23 10:00am PT — technical alignment with Tom + Lifeline network team. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — hosting options and constraints

Adding a quick sizing note ahead of the call. Numbers are a starting point; we should validate with actual traffic patterns.

Baseline pilot (non-airgapped, VPC-hosted):
- 2x A10G equivalents for inference (multi-model concurrent workload), autoscale to 6 nodes for peak.
- Request latency target: P95 < 250ms for 512 tokens.
- KV cache: Redis / Memcached in-customer account (we can recommend instance classes).

Air-gapped pilot (isolated subnet, no outbound):
- Minimum: 1x A10G equivalent for model runtime + 2x smaller CPU nodes for orchestration/ingest.
- Update model packaging: signed Docker tarball pushed via agreed S3 import process.
- Maintenance windows: weekly patch cadence configurable; emergency patches via signed bundle and manual install instructions.

Network needs (summary):
- Outbound egress to Redwood management plane only for control-plane telemetry (if customer allows). Otherwise, we support fully opaque compute in-customer account with manual troubleshooting steps.
- Required ports: 443 (HTTPS) outbound for control channels; we can also support a proxy-based pull model where no outbound is required after initial import. Exact CIDRs to follow.

I'll prepare a brief one-pager on the air-gap package and a sizing matrix before Wed's call.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick sync — hosting options and constraints

Thanks — this is perfect and aligns with what our security team flagged. Wed 8/23 10am PT works for us.

A few clarifications from our side before the call:
- For customer-managed KMS: our compliance team needs an explicit flow diagram showing where keys are used, and whether Redwood ever has plaintext access to tokens or model artifacts.
- For the air-gap model: confirm whether the signed Docker tarball approach requires any runtime daemon to contact Redwood for licensing checks. We prefer no periodic outbound calls.
- On logs: we prefer S3 push to our account with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and a single manifest file that matches daily exports.

Tom (network) — I added you on the invite. Please bring any firewall rules that might block PrivateLink/TGW.

See you tomorrow.

— Priya
Director, Cloud Security, Lifeline Health
